input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) is a blanket mutual bar on assignment without consent, with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, and Section 3(c) separately prohibits Sparkling from assigning at all absent Garman's written authorization. That is walk-away territory under the rule (blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out) and fails every fallback element. Section 17 contains no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so no cure is needed there. We target the fallback: successor assignment by either party on written notice, with consent to other assignments not unreasonably withheld, and a conforming edit to Section 3(c) so the retained use restriction does not contradict the new right.

mappings.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
A successor assignment requires written notice.
Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Permit successor assignment on notice by either party; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld; conform Section 3(c).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a blanket bar on assignment with no M&A carve-out, so Section 20(d) now lets either party assign to a successor to its business or assets on written notice, with consent to any other assignment not to be unreasonably withheld. We also conform Section 3(c) so the use restrictions no longer contradict that right.

ops.oldText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
ops.newText: (d) Either party may assign this Agreement to a successor to its business or assets on written notice to the other party; any other assignment requires the written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
